# Synthetic rtnetlink prefix fixtures

These are synthetic Linux x86-64 little-endian rtnetlink datagrams, generated by
`build.py` using Python's standard library. They contain no captured host data.
The bytes model the Linux UAPI `nlmsghdr`, `ifaddrmsg`, `rtmsg`, `rtattr` and
`rtnexthop` layouts. Every file contains one complete multipart dump ending in
`NLMSG_DONE` with status zero; sequence is 7 and recipient port is 4242.

| File | Cases |
|---|---|
| `ipv4-addresses.hex` | Canonical masking, duplicate network, point-to-point local/peer, assigned `/0` |
| `ipv6-addresses.hex` | IPv6, link-local, tentative address, point-to-point local/peer |
| `ipv4-routes.hex` | Default, table 1000 override, multipath with a dead path, unresolved nexthop object in table 2000, blackhole |
| `ipv6-routes.hex` | Default, link-local, source-specific route in table 500, multipath |

`TestHostPrefixSyntheticWireFixtures` checks exact expected canonical prefixes,
source/interface/table provenance, warning count and deterministic order. Other
native-endian tests synthesize malformed, interrupted, truncated and incomplete
responses and exercise parser resource bounds and cancellation. The fixture test
is skipped on big-endian systems; the generated decoder tests still apply.

Regenerate with `python3 tests/fixtures/network-prefixes/build.py`. The checked-in
`SHA256SUMS` records the generator and hex-file hashes. The generator only writes
these four hex files beneath its own directory and never queries the host.

These fixtures are unit evidence for NET-06's overlap inputs. They do not prove
real LAN/VPN routing, packet isolation, IPv6 RA behavior or release qualification.
